body_ar: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم الحمد لله رب العالمين وأصلي وأسلم على من بعث رحمة للعالمين وعلى آله وأصحابه ومن اهتدى بهديه واستن بسنته إلى يوم الدين يقول المؤلف رحمه الله تعالى: باب معرفة الوقوف عقد هذا الباب لبيان أمر مهم من أمور التجويد وهو حكم الوقف والابتداء، والوقف في اللغة مصدر وقف تستعمل لازمة وتستعمل متعدية، فيقال وقف فلان في الصلاة أي قام، ويقال وقف فلان راحلته أو ناقته إذا حبسها، ومنه قول عنترة
body_en:
In the name of God, the Most Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise be to God, Lord of the worlds. I invoke blessings and peace upon him who was sent as a mercy to the worlds, and upon his family and his Companions and whoever has taken his guidance for guidance and his sunnah for a way, until the Day of Judgement.

The author (may God, be He exalted, have mercy on him) says: "Chapter on the knowledge of the pauses." He set up this chapter to expound an important matter among the matters of Qur'anic recitation (tajwīd), namely the ruling on pausing and on beginning again. Pausing (waqf), in the language, is the verbal noun of waqafa, which is used both intransitively and transitively. One says "So-and-so waqafa in the prayer", meaning that he stood; and one says "So-and-so waqafa his mount or his she-camel", when he brought it to a halt. And from this is the saying of Antarah

The published page carries only the opening excerpt of this tape; the Arabic breaks off and the full text is offered on the site as a downloadable Word document. The English ends exactly where the Arabic ends. Nothing has been supplied to complete it.

The Arabic breaks off exactly at 'And from this is the saying of Antarah', immediately before the line of verse that was to be cited. The verse is not in the source and nothing has been supplied for it; the English ends at the same point.
The Sheikh here names the topic of the chapter as 'the ruling on pausing and beginning again'. The ruling itself is not given in this excerpt, and the page must not be read as containing it.

al-Jazariyyah is the versified primer on Qur'anic recitation by Ibn al-Jazari, and 'the author' throughout this series is Ibn al-Jazari. The series title is left transliterated and untranslated. Articles 436-446 are tapes of this one series; their tape numbering in the titles does not run in the same order as the article IDs.
